title: FlyDubai Pilot Stabbed by Co-Pilot: Heroic Rescue in Saudi Arabia
summary: The pilot, Smit Machchhar, was stabbed by his co-pilot during an alleged crash attempt, and passengers and crew intervened to stop the attack, leading to the safe landing of the plane in Saudi Arabia. The incident highlights both the bravery of the pilot and the efforts of the crew.

facts.statement: A badly wounded pilot managed to unlock the cockpit door and avert a crash after being stabbed by his co-pilot.
The pilot was hailed as a hero for opening the cockpit door and allowing passengers to overpower the attacker.
The incident occurred in Saudi Arabia and led to a safe landing of the plane.

sources.title: Suicide by plane or terrorism? Speculation over motive in flight 1073 attack
sources.description:
Experts sceptical flydubai co-pilot’s only motivation was to end his own life and say key question is means of radicalisation

At around 9.30 on Wednesday morning local time, Tali Manes was taking her six-year-old daughter, Nina, to the toilet on the regular flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv when she heard a series of heavy blows against the cockpit door.

Manes, an Israeli bank executive, immediately told a flight attendant seated nearby that something was wrong. When he did not react, she shouted at him: “Something is happening in there!” Seconds later, the man “simply went to the [cockpit] door and opened it”, Manes told Israel’s Channel 12 TV.

sources.title: ‘I was fighting for my life’: Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls flydubai cockpit attack
sources.description:
Smit Machchhar says in video call with Indian PM that he realised if he did not get up ‘passengers would lose their lives’

The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv said his faith and his desire to save his passengers allowed him to make a “last push” to open the cockpit door as he fought for his life.

Capt Smit Machchhar, who was recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, described to India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, how he helped save the plane and its more than 170 passengers.

sources.title: I was determined not to let others die, Captain Smit tells PM Modi
sources.description:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday spoke to Captain Smit Machchaar, who foiled an attempt by his co-pilot to allegedly crash an Israel-bound flydubai flight, and applauded his bravery.
During the telephonic conversation, Machchaar gave details of his experience and what gave him courage during the incident, government sources said.
Modi applauded the pilot's bravery and wished him a quick recovery, the sources said.
The prime minister on Thursday had said in the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, Machchhar showed immense courage and unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others.
Modi said Machchhar is a "HERO" and his valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy.
Addressing the centenary celebrations of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), the prime minister had also said that the pilot of the flydubai flight showed great patience, acumen and bravery.

sources.title: Deeply concerned: UN chief Guterres strongly condemns flydubai attack
sources.description:
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has expressed deep concern over an incident aboard a flydubai flight in which an Indian pilot sustained serious injuries while foiling an alleged attempt by his co-pilot to crash the aircraft.
The Dubai to Tel Aviv flight, carrying 174 people, including 27 children, made an emergency landing at Tabuk in northwest Saudi Arabia on Wednesday following an altercation in the cockpit.
The co-pilot, identified by Israeli officials as an Omani national, stabbed Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar and sent the jet plunging nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds.
Guterres is deeply concerned by the serious incident involving a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight and is relieved that tragedy was averted, a statement issued by the Secretary-General's spokesman Stephane Dujarric said Wednesday.
